    40→  Serial.println("(Using GPIO from PinOut: IO2, IO4, IO18)\n");
    41→  Serial.println("Configuring I2S...\n");
    42→
    43→  // I2S configuration for single INMP441

    45→    .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX),
    46→    .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
    47→    .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,
    48→    .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,  // Single mic on LEFT channel

    62→    .data_in_num = I2S_DIN_PIN
    63→  };
    64→
    65→  esp_err_t err = i2s_driver_install(I2S_PORT, &i2s_config, 0, NULL);
    66→  if (err != ESP_OK) {

    99→    }

   111→
   112→void printBar(int32_t value, int32_t max_val) {

     1→# INMP441 Pin Test Guide
     2→
     3→## Quick Start
     4→
     5→1. **Upload the sketch** `mic_pin_test.ino` to your ESP32-S3-LCD-2
     6→2. **Open Serial Monitor** at 115200 baud
     7→3. **Wire both microphones** according to the pin configuration
     8→4. **Test each mic** by tapping or blowing on them individually
     9→
    10→## Expected Behavior
    11→
    12→✅ **WORKING**: You should see:
    13→- Two bar graphs labeled LEFT and RIGHT
    14→- LEFT bar grows when you tap/blow on mic #1 (L/R=GND)
    15→- RIGHT bar grows when you tap/blow on mic #2 (L/R=VDD)
    16→- Both bars respond independently
    17→
    18→❌ **NOT WORKING**: Signs of problems:
    19→- No bars at all → Check power/ground connections
    20→- Both bars always identical → Check L/R pin connections
    21→- One bar always zero → Check that specific mic's wiring
    22→- Random noise only → Normal for quiet room, make sound!
    23→
    24→## Pin Configuration Options
    25→
    26→### Recommended (Default in sketch):
    27→```
    28→BCK (Bit Clock):    GPIO 2
    29→WS  (Word Select):  GPIO 4
    30→DIN (Data In):      GPIO 18
    31→```
    32→
    33→**IMPORTANT LIMITATIONS:**
    34→- GPIO 19, 20: Occupied by USB (USB_N, USB_P)
    35→- GPIO 33-37: NOT broken out to pin headers (internal only)
    36→- GPIO 2, 4: Camera pins (safe to use if camera not attached)
    37→
    38→### Available Alternatives on ESP32-S3-LCD-2:
    39→
    40→**Pins broken out to headers** (from PinOut in schematic):
    41→- IO2, IO4, IO6, IO7, IO8, IO9, IO10, IO11, IO12, IO13, IO14, IO15, IO16, IO17, IO18, IO21, IO43, IO44, IO47, IO48
    42→
    43→**Truly free pins** (no camera attached):
    44→- **GPIO 18** - Free, not assigned
    45→- **GPIO 2, 4, 6-17** - Camera pins (safe if camera not attached)
    46→
    47→**Avoid these** (already in use):
    48→- GPIO 0 (BOOT), 1 (BL), 5 (BAT) - System pins
    49→- GPIO 19, 20 (USB_N, USB_P) - USB occupied
    50→- GPIO 33-37 - **NOT broken out to headers!**
    51→- GPIO 38-42, 45 (SPI/LCD/SD) - Display/SD card
    52→- GPIO 43, 44 (U0_TXD, U0_RXD) - Serial console
    53→- GPIO 46 (TP_INT) - Touch panel interrupt
    54→- GPIO 47, 48 (I2C) - IMU and touch panel
    55→
    56→## How to Test Different Pins
    57→
    58→1. **Edit lines in the sketch** (line numbers vary by sketch):
    59→   ```cpp
    60→   #define I2S_BCK_PIN   2     // Try different pin here
    61→   #define I2S_WS_PIN    4     // Try different pin here
    62→   #define I2S_DIN_PIN   18    // Try different pin here
    63→   ```
    64→
    65→   **Alternative pin combinations** (if camera not attached):
    66→   - 18, 2, 4 (default)
    67→   - 6, 7, 8
    68→   - 10, 11, 12
    69→
    70→2. **Re-upload** and check Serial Monitor
    71→3. **Note which pins work** for your final implementation
    72→
    73→## Sketch Options
    74→
    75→### `mic_pin_test.ino` - Dual Microphone Test
    76→- Tests TWO INMP441 microphones in stereo configuration
    77→- LEFT mic: L/R pin → GND
    78→- RIGHT mic: L/R pin → VDD
    79→- Good for validating stereo recording setup
    80→
    81→### `single_mic_test.ino` - Single Microphone Test
    82→- Tests ONE INMP441 microphone
    83→- Simpler wiring and validation
    84→- Use this first to verify basic I2S functionality
    85→- Wire mic L/R pin → GND
    86→
    87→## Wiring Diagram
    88→
    89→### Dual Microphone (stereo):
    90→```
    91→ESP32-S3-LCD-2                INMP441 #1 (LEFT)       INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
    92→──────────────                ─────────────────       ──────────────────
    93→3.3V ────────────┬──────────── VDD                    VDD
    94→                 │
    95→GND ─────────────┼──────────── GND ──────────────┬─── GND
    96→                 │                                │
    97→GPIO 2 (BCK) ────┼──────────── SCK ───────────────┼─── SCK
    98→                 │                                │
    99→GPIO 4 (WS) ─────┼──────────── WS ────────────────┼─── WS
   100→                 │                                │
   101→GPIO 18 (DIN) ───┴──────────── SD ────────────────┴─── SD
   102→                                │                     │
   103→                                L/R ──> GND           L/R ──> 3.3V
   104→                                      (LEFT)                (RIGHT)
   105→```
   106→
   107→### Single Microphone (mono):
   108→```
   109→ESP32-S3-LCD-2                INMP441
   110→──────────────                ─────────
   111→3.3V ────────────────────────── VDD
   112→GND ─────────────┬───────────── GND
   113→                 │
   114→GPIO 2 (BCK) ────┼───────────── SCK
   115→GPIO 4 (WS) ─────┼───────────── WS
   116→GPIO 18 (DIN) ───┴───────────── SD
   117→                                │
   118→                                L/R ──> GND (for LEFT)
   119→                                    or  3.3V (for RIGHT)
   120→```
   121→
   122→## Troubleshooting
   123→
   124→### "ERROR: i2s_driver_install failed"
   125→- Pin conflict with another peripheral
   126→- Try different GPIO pins
   127→
   128→### "ERROR: i2s_set_pin failed"
   129→- Invalid pin number
   130→- Check ESP32-S3 GPIO matrix limitations
   131→
   132→### Both channels show identical signals
   133→- L/R pins not configured correctly
   134→- Check: Mic #1 L/R → GND, Mic #2 L/R → VDD
   135→
   136→### Very low signal levels (< 1000)
   137→- Normal for quiet environment
   138→- Try clapping or speaking loudly close to mic
   139→- Good levels: 10,000 - 1,000,000+ for loud sounds
   140→
   141→### One channel always zero
   142→- Check that specific microphone's power/ground
   143→- Verify SD line connection
   144→- Try swapping the two mics to isolate bad unit

/*
 * INMP441 Dual Microphone SD Card Recording Test
 *
 * Records 30 seconds of stereo audio from two INMP441 microphones
 * and saves it as a WAV file to the FFat partition.
 *
 * Hardware Wiring:
 * ================
 * ESP32-S3-LCD-2          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)      INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
 * ────────────────        ─────────────────      ──────────────────
 * 3.3V ───────────┬────── VDD                    VDD
 *                 │
 * GND ────────────┼────── GND ──────────┬─────── GND
 *                 │                     │
 * GPIO 2 (BCK) ───┼────── SCK ──────────┼─────── SCK
 * GPIO 4 (WS) ────┼────── WS ───────────┼─────── WS
 * GPIO 18 (DIN) ──┴────── SD ───────────┴─────── SD
 *                         │                      │
 *                         L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
 *                           (LEFT)                 (RIGHT)
 *
 * Behavior:
 * =========
 * 1. On boot, mounts FFat filesystem
 * 2. Initializes I2S in stereo mode
 * 3. Records 30 seconds of audio
 * 4. Saves as /recording.wav
 * 5. Prints completion message
 * 6. Enters idle loop
 *
 * Output File:
 * ============
 * Format: WAV (PCM)
 * Sample Rate: 16000 Hz
 * Channels: 2 (Stereo)
 * Bit Depth: 16-bit
 * Duration: 30 seconds
 * Size: ~1.92 MB
 */

#include <driver/i2s.h>
#include <FFat.h>

// I2S Pin Configuration
#define I2S_BCK_PIN   2     // Bit Clock
#define I2S_WS_PIN    4     // Word Select
#define I2S_DIN_PIN   18    // Data In

// Recording Configuration
#define I2S_PORT        I2S_NUM_0
#define SAMPLE_RATE     16000
#define CHANNELS        2
#define BITS_PER_SAMPLE 16
#define RECORD_DURATION 30     // seconds
#define BUFFER_SIZE     2048   // samples (int16_t stereo pairs)

// Calculate total samples
const uint32_t TOTAL_SAMPLES = SAMPLE_RATE * CHANNELS * RECORD_DURATION;
const uint32_t WAV_DATA_SIZE = TOTAL_SAMPLES * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8);
const uint32_t WAV_FILE_SIZE = WAV_DATA_SIZE + 36;  // 44 byte header - 8

// LED for visual feedback
#define LED_PIN 1  // Backlight pin

// Buffers
int32_t i2s_buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];      // I2S read buffer (32-bit samples)
int16_t wav_buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];      // WAV write buffer (16-bit samples)

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);  // LED on during setup

  Serial.println("\n========================================");
  Serial.println("INMP441 Dual Mic SD Recording Test");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  // Mount FFat filesystem
  Serial.print("Mounting FFat... ");
  if (!FFat.begin(true)) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    Serial.println("ERROR: Cannot mount FFat partition");
    Serial.println("Run upload_to_flash.sh to format the partition");
    while(1) {
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
      delay(200);
    }
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Print filesystem info
  Serial.printf("FFat Total: %u bytes\n", FFat.totalBytes());
  Serial.printf("FFat Used: %u bytes\n", FFat.usedBytes());
  Serial.printf("FFat Free: %u bytes\n\n", FFat.totalBytes() - FFat.usedBytes());

  // Initialize I2S
  Serial.print("Initializing I2S... ");
  i2s_config_t i2s_config = {
    .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX),
    .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
    .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,  // INMP441 outputs 24-bit in 32-bit words
    .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_RIGHT_LEFT,  // Stereo
    .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
    .intr_alloc_flags = ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1,
    .dma_buf_count = 4,
    .dma_buf_len = 1024,
    .use_apll = false,
    .tx_desc_auto_clear = false,
    .fixed_mclk = 0
  };

  i2s_pin_config_t pin_config = {
    .bck_io_num = I2S_BCK_PIN,
    .ws_io_num = I2S_WS_PIN,
    .data_out_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
    .data_in_num = I2S_DIN_PIN
  };

  esp_err_t err = i2s_driver_install(I2S_PORT, &i2s_config, 0, NULL);
  if (err != ESP_OK) {
    Serial.printf("FAILED (err=%d)\n", err);
    while(1) delay(1000);
  }

  err = i2s_set_pin(I2S_PORT, &pin_config);
  if (err != ESP_OK) {
    Serial.printf("FAILED (err=%d)\n", err);
    while(1) delay(1000);
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Start recording
  Serial.printf("\nRecording %d seconds of stereo audio...\n", RECORD_DURATION);
  Serial.printf("Target file: /recording.wav\n");
  Serial.printf("Expected size: %u bytes\n\n", WAV_DATA_SIZE + 44);

  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);  // LED off before recording
  delay(500);

  bool success = recordAudio();

  if (success) {
    Serial.println("\n========================================");
    Serial.println("Recording complete!");
    Serial.println("========================================");
    Serial.println("\nFile saved to FFat partition as /recording.wav");
    Serial.println("You can download it using upload_to_flash.sh");
    Serial.println("or access via FFat filesystem.");
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);  // LED on = success
  } else {
    Serial.println("\n========================================");
    Serial.println("Recording FAILED!");
    Serial.println("========================================");
    // LED will blink in loop()
  }
}

void loop() {
  // Idle - blink LED slowly if failed
  if (digitalRead(LED_PIN) == LOW) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(500);
  } else {
    delay(1000);
  }
}

bool recordAudio() {
  // Open file for writing
  File file = FFat.open("/recording.wav", FILE_WRITE);
  if (!file) {
    Serial.println("ERROR: Cannot create file");
    return false;
  }

  // Write WAV header
  writeWavHeader(file, WAV_DATA_SIZE);

  // Recording loop
  uint32_t samples_written = 0;
  uint32_t last_percent = 0;
  unsigned long start_time = millis();

  while (samples_written < TOTAL_SAMPLES) {
    // Blink LED during recording
    if ((millis() / 200) % 2 == 0) {
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
    } else {
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
    }

    // Read I2S data
    size_t bytes_read = 0;
    esp_err_t err = i2s_read(I2S_PORT, i2s_buffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(int32_t),
                             &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY);

    if (err != ESP_OK) {
      Serial.printf("\nERROR: I2S read failed (err=%d)\n", err);
      file.close();
      return false;
    }

    // Convert 32-bit to 16-bit
    int samples_read = bytes_read / sizeof(int32_t);
    for (int i = 0; i < samples_read; i++) {
      // INMP441 outputs 24-bit data in upper bits of 32-bit word
      // Shift right by 16 to get 16-bit output (keeping MSBs)
      wav_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);
    }

    // Write to file
    size_t bytes_written = file.write((uint8_t*)wav_buffer, samples_read * sizeof(int16_t));
    if (bytes_written != samples_read * sizeof(int16_t)) {
      Serial.printf("\nERROR: File write failed (wrote %u of %u bytes)\n",
                    bytes_written, samples_read * sizeof(int16_t));
      file.close();
      return false;
    }

    samples_written += samples_read;

    // Print progress
    uint32_t percent = (samples_written * 100) / TOTAL_SAMPLES;
    if (percent != last_percent && percent % 10 == 0) {
      unsigned long elapsed = millis() - start_time;
      Serial.printf("Progress: %u%% (%u / %u samples, %lu ms)\n",
                    percent, samples_written, TOTAL_SAMPLES, elapsed);
      last_percent = percent;
    }
  }

  file.close();

  unsigned long total_time = millis() - start_time;
  Serial.printf("\nRecording finished: %u samples in %lu ms\n", samples_written, total_time);

  return true;
}

void writeWavHeader(File &file, uint32_t data_size) {
  // RIFF header
  file.write((uint8_t*)"RIFF", 4);
  uint32_t file_size = data_size + 36;
  writeLittleEndian(file, file_size, 4);
  file.write((uint8_t*)"WAVE", 4);

  // fmt chunk
  file.write((uint8_t*)"fmt ", 4);
  writeLittleEndian(file, 16, 4);                    // Chunk size
  writeLittleEndian(file, 1, 2);                     // Audio format (1 = PCM)
  writeLittleEndian(file, CHANNELS, 2);              // Number of channels
  writeLittleEndian(file, SAMPLE_RATE, 4);           // Sample rate
  writeLittleEndian(file, SAMPLE_RATE * CHANNELS * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8), 4); // Byte rate
  writeLittleEndian(file, CHANNELS * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8), 2); // Block align
  writeLittleEndian(file, BITS_PER_SAMPLE, 2);       // Bits per sample

  // data chunk
  file.write((uint8_t*)"data", 4);
  writeLittleEndian(file, data_size, 4);
}

void writeLittleEndian(File &file, uint32_t value, int bytes) {
  for (int i = 0; i < bytes; i++) {
    file.write((uint8_t)(value & 0xFF));
    value >>= 8;
  }
}

```md
# INMP441 Dual Microphone SD Recording Test - Wiring Guide

## Overview

This test records 30 seconds of stereo audio from two INMP441 microphones and saves it as a WAV file to the ESP32's FFat partition on boot.

## Hardware Requirements

- ESP32-S3-LCD-2 development board
- 2× INMP441 MEMS microphones
- Breadboard and jumper wires
- FFat partition formatted on ESP32 (use `upload_to_flash.sh`)

## Pin Connections

### ESP32-S3-LCD-2 to INMP441 Microphones

\```
ESP32-S3-LCD-2          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)      INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
────────────────        ─────────────────      ──────────────────
3.3V ───────────┬────── VDD                    VDD
                │
GND ────────────┼────── GND ──────────┬─────── GND
                │                     │
GPIO 2 (BCK) ───┼────── SCK ──────────┼─────── SCK
GPIO 4 (WS) ────┼────── WS ───────────┼─────── WS
GPIO 18 (DIN) ──┴────── SD ───────────┴─────── SD
                        │                      │
                        L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
                          (LEFT)                 (RIGHT)
\```

### Pin Summary

| ESP32 Pin | INMP441 Pin | Function           | Notes                          |
|-----------|-------------|--------------------|--------------------------------|
| 3.3V      | VDD         | Power Supply       | Both mics connected in parallel|
| GND       | GND         | Ground             | Both mics connected in parallel|
| GPIO 2    | SCK         | I2S Bit Clock      | Shared by both microphones     |
| GPIO 4    | WS          | I2S Word Select    | Shared by both microphones     |
| GPIO 18   | SD          | I2S Serial Data    | Shared by both microphones     |
| —         | L/R (Mic #1)| Channel Select     | Connect to **GND** for LEFT    |
| —         | L/R (Mic #2)| Channel Select     | Connect to **3.3V** for RIGHT  |

### Critical: L/R Pin Configuration

The **L/R pin** on each INMP441 determines which stereo channel it transmits on:

- **INMP441 #1**: L/R → **GND** (transmits on **LEFT** channel)
- **INMP441 #2**: L/R → **3.3V** (transmits on **RIGHT** channel)

**Do not leave L/R floating!** This will cause unpredictable behavior.

## Pin Selection Rationale

From the ESP32-S3-LCD-2 schematic:

- **GPIO 2, 4**: Camera interface pins (safe to use when camera not attached)
- **GPIO 18**: Free GPIO, not assigned to any peripheral
- These pins are broken out to the board's pin headers
- Compatible with I2S peripheral routing on ESP32-S3

## Recording Specifications

| Parameter       | Value              |
|-----------------|--------------------|
| Sample Rate     | 16,000 Hz          |
| Channels        | 2 (Stereo)         |
| Bit Depth       | 16-bit PCM         |
| Duration        | 30 seconds         |
| File Format     | WAV                |
| File Size       | ~1.92 MB           |
| Output File     | `/recording.wav`   |
| Storage         | FFat partition     |

## Usage Instructions

### 1. Prepare FFat Partition

Before running this sketch, ensure your ESP32 has a formatted FFat partition:

\```bash
cd /home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/working_protos/01_llm_inference_stories260k
./upload_to_flash.sh
\```

This script formats the FFat partition at the correct offset.

### 2. Wire the Microphones

Follow the pin connections table above. **Critical points:**

- Connect both microphones' **SCK**, **WS**, and **SD** pins together (I2S bus)
- **Mic #1 L/R → GND** (for left channel)
- **Mic #2 L/R → 3.3V** (for right channel)
- Ensure solid power and ground connections

### 3. Upload the Sketch

1. Open `dual_mic_sd_record.ino` in Arduino IDE
2. Select **Board**: ESP32S3 Dev Module
3. Select **Partition Scheme**: 16MB Flash (3MB APP/9MB FATFS)
4. Select **PSRAM**: OPI PSRAM
5. Upload the sketch

### 4. Monitor Recording

Open Serial Monitor at **115200 baud**. You should see:

\```
========================================
INMP441 Dual Mic SD Recording Test
========================================

Mounting FFat... OK
FFat Total: 10321920 bytes
FFat Used: 0 bytes
FFat Free: 10321920 bytes

Initializing I2S... OK

Recording 30 seconds of stereo audio...
Target file: /recording.wav
Expected size: 1920044 bytes

Progress: 10% (192000 / 960000 samples, 3000 ms)
Progress: 20% (384000 / 960000 samples, 6000 ms)
Progress: 30% (576000 / 960000 samples, 9000 ms)
...
Progress: 100% (960000 / 960000 samples, 30000 ms)

Recording finished: 960000 samples in 30012 ms

========================================
Recording complete!
========================================

File saved to FFat partition as /recording.wav
\```

### 5. LED Feedback

- **Blinking during recording**: Normal operation
- **Solid ON after completion**: Recording successful
- **Blinking after completion**: Recording failed (check Serial Monitor)

## Retrieving the Recording

The WAV file is stored in the ESP32's FFat partition. To retrieve it:

### Option 1: Using FFat File Browser

If you have an MCP server or file browser that can access the FFat partition, navigate to `/recording.wav`.

### Option 2: Modify Sketch to Stream via Serial

Add code to read the file and send it via Serial (base64 encoded).

### Option 3: Use esptool to Read Partition

\```bash
esptool.py --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/ttyUSB0 read_flash 0x610000 0x9E0000 ffat_dump.bin
\```

Then mount `ffat_dump.bin` as a FAT filesystem on your computer.

## Testing the Recording

To verify both microphones are working:

1. **During recording**, tap or speak near each microphone separately
2. After retrieving `/recording.wav`, play it back on your computer
3. **Left channel** should have audio from **Mic #1** (L/R → GND)
4. **Right channel** should have audio from **Mic #2** (L/R → 3.3V)

Use an audio editor like Audacity to view the stereo waveforms separately.

## Troubleshooting

### "Mounting FFat... FAILED"

- FFat partition not formatted
- Run `upload_to_flash.sh` from the `01_llm_inference_stories260k` example
- Check partition table matches `app3M_fat9M_16MB.csv`

### "ERROR: Cannot create file"

- FFat partition full
- Delete old files or reformat the partition

### "ERROR: I2S read failed"

- Incorrect pin connections
- Check GPIO 2, 4, 18 are correctly wired
- Verify I2S peripheral not in use by other code

### "ERROR: File write failed"

- FFat partition full or corrupted
- Reformat FFat partition

### No audio in one channel

- Check L/R pin on that microphone
  - Mic #1 (left) L/R should be at **GND**
  - Mic #2 (right) L/R should be at **3.3V**
- Verify SCK, WS, SD connections to that mic

### Very low audio levels

- Normal for quiet environments
- Speak loudly or clap near microphones during recording
- INMP441 has high sensitivity; adjust gain in post-processing if needed

### Recording stops early

- I2S buffer overflow (unlikely with current settings)
- SD write speed too slow (check FFat health)

## Next Steps

Once you've verified stereo recording works:

1. Integrate with audio processing algorithms
2. Add VAD (Voice Activity Detection) to trigger recording
3. Implement real-time audio streaming
4. Add compression (e.g., OPUS, MP3) to reduce file size
5. Combine with speaker output for full audio I/O

## Reference

- **INMP441 Datasheet**: I2S MEMS microphone specifications
- **ESP32-S3 I2S Documentation**: ESP-IDF I2S driver API
- **CLAUDE.md**: Pin assignments and board architecture
- **Related Tests**:
  - `single_mic_test/`: Single INMP441 test
  - `mic_pin_test/`: Dual INMP441 pin validation (no SD)

## What I Created

### 📁 File Structure
```
workbench/tests/dual_mic_sd_record/

### 🔌 Pin Layout

**Critical Wiring:**

| ESP32 Pin | INMP441 Connection | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| **3.3V** | VDD (both mics) | Power |
| **GND** | GND (both mics) | Ground |
| **GPIO 2** | SCK (both mics) | I2S Bit Clock |
| **GPIO 4** | WS (both mics) | I2S Word Select |
| **GPIO 18** | SD (both mics) | I2S Serial Data |
| — | **Mic #1 L/R → GND** | LEFT channel |
| — | **Mic #2 L/R → 3.3V** | RIGHT channel |

### 🎯 How It Works

1. **On boot** → Mounts FFat partition
2. **Initializes I2S** in stereo mode (I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_RIGHT_LEFT)
3. **Records 30 seconds** of audio automatically
4. **Saves as** `/recording.wav` (16kHz, 16-bit, stereo, ~1.92MB)
5. **LED feedback**: Blinks during recording, solid ON when complete
6. **Progress updates** every 10% via Serial Monitor (115200 baud)

### 🚀 Quick Start

1. **Format FFat** (if not already done):
   ```bash
   cd workbench/working_protos/01_llm_inference_stories260k
   ./upload_to_flash.sh
   ```

2. **Wire both microphones** following the pin layout above

3. **Upload sketch** in Arduino IDE:
   - Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
   - Partition: 16MB Flash (3MB APP/9MB FATFS)
   - PSRAM: OPI PSRAM

4. **Open Serial Monitor** at 115200 baud and watch the recording progress

### 📊 Recording Specs

- **Sample Rate**: 16,000 Hz
- **Channels**: 2 (Stereo)
- **Bit Depth**: 16-bit PCM
- **Duration**: 30 seconds
- **Format**: WAV with proper header
- **Size**: 1,920,044 bytes

The sketch uses streaming writes (4KB chunks) to avoid memory overflow, converting from 32-bit I2S samples to 16-bit WAV format on-the-fly.

All documentation is in the WIRING_GUIDE.md file!

Yes, you only need **ONE 3.3V pin** from your board! This is correct.

The 3.3V pin connects to:
1. **VDD on Mic #1** (power)
2. **VDD on Mic #2** (power)  
3. **L/R on Mic #2** (channel select = RIGHT)

All three connect to the **same 3.3V pin** on your ESP32 board.

Similarly, your **one GND pin** connects to:
1. **GND on Mic #1**
2. **GND on Mic #2**
3. **L/R on Mic #1** (channel select = LEFT)

## Clearer Wiring Diagram

```
ESP32-S3-LCD-2 Board          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)    INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
                              ─────────────────    ──────────────────
                    ┌──────── VDD                  VDD ───┐
                    │                                      │
3.3V (ONE PIN) ─────┼──────────────────────────────────────┼─── L/R (Mic #2)
                    │                                      │
                    │                              
GND (ONE PIN) ──────┼──────── GND                  GND     
                    │         │                    
                    │         └─ L/R (Mic #1)
                    │
GPIO 2 (BCK) ───────┼──────── SCK ──────────────── SCK
GPIO 4 (WS) ────────┼──────── WS ───────────────── WS  
GPIO 18 (DIN) ──────┴──────── SD ───────────────── SD
```

## On a Breadboard

If using a breadboard, you'd typically:

1. Connect the ESP32's **3.3V pin** to the breadboard's **+ rail**
2. Connect the ESP32's **GND pin** to the breadboard's **- rail**

Then connect:
- Both mics' **VDD** → breadboard **+ rail** (3.3V)
- Both mics' **GND** → breadboard **- rail** (GND)
- Mic #1 **L/R** → breadboard **- rail** (GND = LEFT)
- Mic #2 **L/R** → breadboard **+ rail** (3.3V = RIGHT)

This way everything shares the same power/ground rails, which is perfectly fine!

   169→
   170→bool recordAudio() {
   171→  // Open file for writing
   172→  File file = FFat.open("/recording.wav", FILE_WRITE);
   173→  if (!file) {
   174→    Serial.println("ERROR: Cannot create file");
   175→    return false;
   176→  }
   177→
   178→  // Write WAV header
   179→  writeWavHeader(file, WAV_DATA_SIZE);
   180→
   181→  // Recording loop
   182→  uint32_t samples_written = 0;
   183→  uint32_t last_percent = 0;
   184→  unsigned long start_time = millis();
   185→
   186→  while (samples_written < TOTAL_SAMPLES) {
   187→    // Blink LED during recording
   188→    if ((millis() / 200) % 2 == 0) {
   189→      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   190→    } else {
   191→      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
   192→    }
   193→
   194→    // Read I2S data
   195→    size_t bytes_read = 0;
   196→    esp_err_t err = i2s_read(I2S_PORT, i2s_buffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(int32_t),
   197→                             &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY);
   198→
   199→    if (err != ESP_OK) {
   200→      Serial.printf("\nERROR: I2S read failed (err=%d)\n", err);
   201→      file.close();
   202→      return false;
   203→    }
   204→
   205→    // Convert 32-bit to 16-bit
   206→    int samples_read = bytes_read / sizeof(int32_t);
   207→    for (int i = 0; i < samples_read; i++) {
   208→      // INMP441 outputs 24-bit data in upper bits of 32-bit word
   209→      // Shift right by 16 to get 16-bit output (keeping MSBs)
   210→      wav_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);
   211→    }
   212→
   213→    // Write to file
   214→    size_t bytes_written = file.write((uint8_t*)wav_buffer, samples_read * sizeof(int16_t));
   215→    if (bytes_written != samples_read * sizeof(int16_t)) {
   216→      Serial.printf("\nERROR: File write failed (wrote %u of %u bytes)\n",
   217→                    bytes_written, samples_read * sizeof(int16_t));
   218→      file.close();
   219→      return false;
   220→    }
   221→
   222→    samples_written += samples_read;
   223→
   224→    // Print progress
   225→    uint32_t percent = (samples_written * 100) / TOTAL_SAMPLES;
   226→    if (percent != last_percent && percent % 10 == 0) {
   227→      unsigned long elapsed = millis() - start_time;
   228→      Serial.printf("Progress: %u%% (%u / %u samples, %lu ms)\n",
   229→                    percent, samples_written, TOTAL_SAMPLES, elapsed);
   230→      last_percent = percent;
   231→    }
   232→  }
   233→
   234→  file.close();
   235→
   236→  unsigned long total_time = millis() - start_time;
   237→  Serial.printf("\nRecording finished: %u samples in %lu ms\n", samples_written, total_time);
   238→
   239→  return true;
   240→}
   241→
   242→void writeWavHeader(File &file, uint32_t data_size) {
   243→  // RIFF header
   244→  file.write((uint8_t*)"RIFF", 4);
   245→  uint32_t file_size = data_size + 36;
   246→  writeLittleEndian(file, file_size, 4);
   247→  file.write((uint8_t*)"WAVE", 4);
   248→
   249→  // fmt chunk
   250→  file.write((uint8_t*)"fmt ", 4);
   251→  writeLittleEndian(file, 16, 4);                    // Chunk size
   252→  writeLittleEndian(file, 1, 2);                     // Audio format (1 = PCM)
   253→  writeLittleEndian(file, CHANNELS, 2);              // Number of channels
   254→  writeLittleEndian(file, SAMPLE_RATE, 4);           // Sample rate
   255→  writeLittleEndian(file, SAMPLE_RATE * CHANNELS * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8), 4); // Byte rate
   256→  writeLittleEndian(file, CHANNELS * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8), 2); // Block align
   257→  writeLittleEndian(file, BITS_PER_SAMPLE, 2);       // Bits per sample
   258→
   259→  // data chunk
   260→  file.write((uint8_t*)"data", 4);
   261→  writeLittleEndian(file, data_size, 4);
   262→}
   263→
   264→void writeLittleEndian(File &file, uint32_t value, int bytes) {
   265→  for (int i = 0; i < bytes; i++) {
   266→    file.write((uint8_t)(value & 0xFF));
   267→    value >>= 8;
   268→  }
   269→}
   270→

Based on the search results, here's how the INMP441 microphone L/R pin works for stereo wiring:

## L/R Pin Configuration

The L/R pin is used to select the left or right channel for stereo applications. Connect this pin to ground for left channel or leave it floating for right channel.

More specifically, according to the official datasheet:
- When set low, the microphone outputs its signal in the left channel of the I²S frame. When set high, the microphone outputs its signal in the right channel.

## Stereo Wiring Setup

For a stereo configuration with two INMP441 microphones:

The L/R pin on the two INMP441s should be set to opposite settings—one pulled to VDD, and the other to ground. When pulled to GND, the microphone will output its data on the left channel of the I2S stream, and when pulled to VDD it will output its data on the right channel.

## Practical Wiring

L/R strap: one mic to GND (Left), the other to 3.3 V (Right).

Both microphones share the same I2S bus connections (SCK, WS, and SD pins can be connected together), while the L/R pin is what differentiates which channel each microphone outputs on.

## Confirmed L/R Pin Configuration

From the INMP441 datasheet and multiple sources:

- **L/R → GND** = **LEFT channel** ✅
- **L/R → VDD (3.3V)** = **RIGHT channel** ✅

So your wiring matches exactly what it should be. The fact that your **right channel is perfect** confirms the I2S bus is working correctly.

## Troubleshooting the Left Mic

Since the right works perfectly but left is just noise, here are the likely culprits:

### 1. **Defective Microphone Module** (Most Likely)
- MEMS microphones can be damaged by static discharge or physical shock
- Try swapping with your spare module - good plan!

### 2. **Check Left Mic Connections**
Verify these specific connections on the **left mic** (L/R → GND):
- **VDD** → Solid 3.3V connection
- **GND** → Solid ground connection  
- **L/R** → Firmly connected to GND (not floating!)
- **SD (Data)** → Connected to GPIO 18 (shared with right mic)

### 3. **Test: Swap the L/R Pins**
Quick diagnostic - temporarily **swap the L/R connections**:
- Left mic: L/R → **3.3V** (becomes right channel)
- Right mic: L/R → **GND** (becomes left channel)

**If the noise follows the physical mic** (now in right channel) → **Bad mic module**  
**If the noise stays in left channel** → **Wiring or ESP32 issue**

### 4. **Single Mic Fallback**
If one mic is bad, you can absolutely use just one! Just change the I2S config:

```cpp
.channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,  // Mono from one mic
```

And keep only the working mic with L/R → GND.

## Let's Debug This Step by Step

### First: Clarify Current Wiring

When you say you "swapped the L/R pins," do you mean:

**Option A:** You physically swapped which wire goes to which mic?
- Mic #1: L/R → **3.3V** (now right channel)
- Mic #2: L/R → **GND** (now left channel)

**Option B:** Both L/R pins are now connected to the same thing?
- Both mics: L/R → GND (both on left channel) ❌
- Both mics: L/R → 3.3V (both on right channel) ❌

### Symptoms Analysis

**"Sound in the middle, not specific to left or right"** strongly suggests:

1. **Both mics outputting on the SAME channel** - They're mixing together, creating a mono-ish sound
2. **L/R pins floating or loose** - Undefined state causing both to act as same channel
3. **One or both L/R connections not solid**

### Quick Diagnostic Test

Can you check **RIGHT NOW** with a multimeter or visually confirm:

**Mic #1 L/R pin:** Connected to what? (GND or 3.3V?)  
**Mic #2 L/R pin:** Connected to what? (GND or 3.3V?)

They **MUST be opposite** for stereo to work:
- ✅ One → GND, Other → 3.3V (correct stereo)
- ❌ Both → GND (both on left channel = mono)
- ❌ Both → 3.3V (both on right channel = mono)
- ❌ Either floating (undefined behavior)

### Expected Behavior for Stereo

When wired correctly, you should hear:
- **Tap left mic** → Audio ONLY in left speaker
- **Tap right mic** → Audio ONLY in right speaker
- **Tap both** → Audio in both speakers

If you're hearing audio "in the middle," it means both mics are being mixed onto one channel.

Let me know the exact current wiring state and we'll fix this!

## Diagnostic Steps

### Test 1: Physical Isolation Test

Record a new 30-second sample but do this:
- **First 10 seconds:** Cover/block **Mic 1** (L/R→GND), speak into **Mic 2** only
- **Next 10 seconds:** Cover/block **Mic 2** (L/R→3.3V), speak into **Mic 1** only  
- **Last 10 seconds:** Speak into both

Then play the recording and check:
- **Seconds 0-10:** Should ONLY be in RIGHT speaker
- **Seconds 10-20:** Should ONLY be in LEFT speaker
- **Seconds 20-30:** Should be in BOTH speakers

### Test 2: Verify in Audacity

Open the recording in Audacity (free audio editor):
1. **View** → **Show Stereo Channels Separate**
2. Look at the waveforms - are they identical or different?
   - **Identical waveforms** = Both mics outputting same signal (hardware issue)
   - **Different waveforms** = Stereo working correctly

### Possible Issues

#### Issue 1: Data Line Crosstalk
Since **GPIO 18 (SD/Data) is shared**, if there's a poor connection or the mics are outputting at the same time incorrectly, they could interfere.

**Quick test:** Temporarily disconnect **Mic 1** entirely (remove all 6 wires). Record with only **Mic 2**. Does it sound clean in the right channel?

#### Issue 2: Bit Shift Problem
The code shifts right by 16 bits. Maybe we need to shift by 8 instead?

Try changing line 210 in the sketch:
```cpp
// Current:
wav_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);

// Try this:
wav_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 8);
```

#### Issue 3: Grounding/Noise
- Are the GND connections solid to BOTH mics?
- Try adding a 0.1µF capacitor between VDD and GND on each mic (close to the mic)

### Quick Question

When you said you "swapped L/R pins" earlier, what exactly changed? The wiring you described now seems like the original wiring. Did you:
- Swap which mic connects to GND vs 3.3V?
- Or swap the physical mic positions?
- Or something else?

Let me know the results of Test 1 (physical isolation) and we'll narrow this down!

However, let's think about the memory requirements:
- 30 seconds at 16kHz, stereo, 16-bit = 1,920,000 bytes = ~1.92 MB
- ESP32-S3 has PSRAM (typically 8MB on the LCD-2 board)
- So we CAN fit this in PSRAM!

The approach would be:
1. Allocate a large buffer in PSRAM (1.92 MB)
2. Record I2S data directly into this buffer
3. When recording complete, write the entire buffer to SD card in one go

This is actually a smart idea because:
- No SD card write latency during recording
- I2S can run at full speed without interruption
- Simpler error handling

Let me modify the sketch to do this.

Perfect! I've completely rewritten the sketch to use **PSRAM buffering** - this eliminates ALL SD card interference during recording!

## What Changed

### New Recording Flow

1. **Allocate ~1.92 MB in PSRAM** (plenty available on ESP32-S3)
2. **Record 30 seconds directly to PSRAM** (no SD card access at all!)
3. **Mount SD card AFTER recording**
4. **Write entire buffer to SD in one go**

### Key Benefits

✅ **Zero SD card timing interference** during I2S recording  
✅ **Maximum I2S stability** - no competing writes  
✅ **Cleaner audio capture** - uninterrupted data stream  
✅ **Simpler error handling** - record and write are separate steps  

### The Code Changes

**Before:**
```cpp
while recording {
  read I2S → convert → write to SD  // SD slows things down!
}
```

**After:**
```cpp
// Step 1: Record (no SD!)
while recording {
  read I2S → convert → write to PSRAM  // Lightning fast!
}

// Step 2: Save (after recording done)
mount SD → write PSRAM buffer to SD → done
```

I found several resources discussing stereo-to-mono downmix practices for voice recording. Here are the key findings:

## Basic Downmix Algorithm

The standard formula for stereo-to-mono downmix is M = L / 2 + R / 2, where the left and right channels are averaged together.

A basic stereo to mono mix involves bussing both L and R tracks to a mono track, ensuring levels are set correctly.

## Phase Issues and Special Cases

A critical consideration for microphone recordings: If downmixing goes silent or very quiet, there may be a phase problem with the input.

The proper way to convert to mono with XLR inputs is to negate one channel and add it to the other channel, which removes crosstalk and interferences. When polarity is inverted on one channel, signals cancel each other out during downmix.

## Mono Compatibility

Professionals should make recordings mono safe, as there are many situations where audio gets downmixed to mono in the real world.

## Volume Considerations

When an input only sends on one channel and you downmix to mono using M = L/2 + R/2, volume will logically be lower, whereas having the same signal on both channels won't show a difference.

The search results indicate there isn't a universally recognized "intelligent" algorithm that automatically fixes mono incompatibility issues in real-time.

## Key Implementations

### ESP32-S3 Dual Microphone Beamforming
A practical guide demonstrates building a two-microphone acoustic direction-finding (DOA) system using the ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 and two INMP441 I2S microphones, acquiring synchronized stereo audio over I2S and estimating time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) with normalized cross-correlation. The implementation configures I2S for stereo capture at 48 kHz (32-bit slots, 24-bit data left-justified), reads frames, deinterleaves Left/Right data, applies simple DC removal, and estimates TDOA via normalized cross-correlation.

### Espressif Official Solutions
ESP-Skainet, Espressif's speech recognition SDK, takes advantage of various acoustic algorithms including voice-activity detection, acoustic echo cancellation, noise reduction and beamforming. The ESP32-S3-Korvo-2 is equipped with a two-microphone array suitable for voice recognition and near/far-field voice wake-up applications.

### Commercial Microphone Arrays
The ReSpeaker Lite Voice Assistant Kit combines a dual-microphone array with the XIAO ESP32S3 module for voice recognition, noise reduction, and processing. The ReSpeaker XVF3800 USB 4-Mic Array is a professional circular microphone array with AEC, beamforming, noise suppression, and 360° voice capture.

### Technical Details
Two microphones can share the same I2S bus, alternating which one is outputting its signal in time with the WS signal, enabling synchronized dual-microphone capture on a single I2S peripheral.

These resources provide both DIY approaches using INMP441 microphones and ready-made solutions like the ReSpeaker kits, all supporting beamforming and noise reduction on ESP32 platforms.

/*
 * INMP441 Dual Microphone to Mono Recording Test
 * With PSRAM Buffering and Smart Downmixing
 *
 * Records from two INMP441 microphones and intelligently downmixes
 * them to MONO for clearer voice capture than a single mic.
 *
 * Hardware Wiring:
 * ================
 * ESP32-S3-LCD-2          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)      INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
 * ────────────────        ─────────────────      ──────────────────
 * 3.3V ───────────┬────── VDD                    VDD
 *                 │
 * GND ────────────┼────── GND ──────────┬─────── GND
 *                 │                     │
 * GPIO 2 (BCK) ───┼────── SCK ──────────┼─────── SCK
 * GPIO 4 (WS) ────┼────── WS ───────────┼─────── WS
 * GPIO 18 (DIN) ──┴────── SD ───────────┴─────── SD
 *                         │                      │
 *                         L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
 *                           (LEFT)                 (RIGHT)
 *
 * Downmixing Algorithms (choose one below):
 * =========================================
 * SIMPLE_AVERAGE:  Mono = (L + R) / 2
 *                  - Standard approach, works well for in-phase signals
 *                  - May have phase cancellation if mics are far apart
 *
 * PEAK_SELECT:     Mono = max(abs(L), abs(R)) with sign preservation
 *                  - Takes the stronger signal at each sample
 *                  - Prevents phase cancellation
 *                  - Better for speech in noisy environments
 *
 * ADAPTIVE_MIX:    Mono = weighted average based on recent signal strength
 *                  - Intelligently favors the mic with better signal
 *                  - Best overall quality for voice capture
 *
 * Behavior:
 * =========
 * 1. Allocates PSRAM buffer for stereo capture
 * 2. Records 30 seconds of stereo audio to PSRAM
 * 3. Downmixes stereo to mono using selected algorithm
 * 4. Writes mono WAV file to SD card
 * 5. LED on = success
 *
 * Output File:
 * ============
 * Format: WAV (PCM)
 * Sample Rate: 16000 Hz
 * Channels: 1 (MONO - downmixed from stereo)
 * Bit Depth: 16-bit
 * Duration: 30 seconds
 * Size: ~960 KB (half of stereo)
 */

#include <driver/i2s.h>
#include "FS.h"
#include "SD.h"
#include "SPI.h"

// Choose downmix algorithm (uncomment ONE)
#define SIMPLE_AVERAGE    // Standard (L+R)/2
// #define PEAK_SELECT    // Take louder channel
// #define ADAPTIVE_MIX   // Intelligent weighted mix

// I2S Pin Configuration
#define I2S_BCK_PIN   2     // Bit Clock
#define I2S_WS_PIN    4     // Word Select
#define I2S_DIN_PIN   18    // Data In

// SD Card SPI Pin Configuration
#define SD_CS    41
#define SD_MOSI  38
#define SD_MISO  40
#define SD_SCK   39

// Recording Configuration
#define I2S_PORT        I2S_NUM_0
#define SAMPLE_RATE     16000
#define BITS_PER_SAMPLE 16
#define RECORD_DURATION 30
#define BUFFER_SIZE     2048

// Calculate sizes
const uint32_t STEREO_SAMPLES = SAMPLE_RATE * 2 * RECORD_DURATION;  // L+R interleaved
const uint32_t MONO_SAMPLES = SAMPLE_RATE * RECORD_DURATION;        // Mono only
const uint32_t MONO_DATA_SIZE = MONO_SAMPLES * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8);

// LED for visual feedback
#define LED_PIN 1

// Buffers
int32_t i2s_buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];      // I2S read buffer (32-bit samples)
int16_t* stereo_buffer = nullptr;     // PSRAM: stereo recording (L,R,L,R,...)
int16_t* mono_buffer = nullptr;       // PSRAM: mono downmix result

#ifdef ADAPTIVE_MIX
// Adaptive mixing state
float left_energy = 0.0f;
float right_energy = 0.0f;
const float ENERGY_DECAY = 0.95f;  // Smooth signal strength tracking
#endif

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);

  Serial.println("\n========================================");
  Serial.println("INMP441 Dual Mic to Mono Recording");
  Serial.println("(Smart Downmix + PSRAM Buffering)");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  // Print selected algorithm
  #ifdef SIMPLE_AVERAGE
  Serial.println("Downmix Algorithm: SIMPLE_AVERAGE (L+R)/2");
  #endif
  #ifdef PEAK_SELECT
  Serial.println("Downmix Algorithm: PEAK_SELECT (louder channel)");
  #endif
  #ifdef ADAPTIVE_MIX
  Serial.println("Downmix Algorithm: ADAPTIVE_MIX (intelligent weighting)");
  #endif
  Serial.println();

  // Check PSRAM
  Serial.printf("Total PSRAM: %u bytes\n", ESP.getPsramSize());
  Serial.printf("Free PSRAM: %u bytes\n", ESP.getFreePsram());

  // Allocate stereo buffer
  uint32_t stereo_bytes = STEREO_SAMPLES * sizeof(int16_t);
  Serial.printf("\nAllocating stereo buffer (%u bytes)... ", stereo_bytes);
  stereo_buffer = (int16_t*)ps_malloc(stereo_bytes);
  if (!stereo_buffer) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Allocate mono buffer
  Serial.printf("Allocating mono buffer (%u bytes)... ", MONO_DATA_SIZE);
  mono_buffer = (int16_t*)ps_malloc(MONO_DATA_SIZE);
  if (!mono_buffer) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK");
  Serial.printf("Free PSRAM after allocation: %u bytes\n\n", ESP.getFreePsram());

  // Initialize I2S
  Serial.print("Initializing I2S... ");
  i2s_config_t i2s_config = {
    .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX),
    .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
    .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,
    .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_RIGHT_LEFT,  // Stereo
    .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
    .intr_alloc_flags = ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1,
    .dma_buf_count = 4,
    .dma_buf_len = 1024,
    .use_apll = false,
    .tx_desc_auto_clear = false,
    .fixed_mclk = 0
  };

  i2s_pin_config_t pin_config = {
    .bck_io_num = I2S_BCK_PIN,
    .ws_io_num = I2S_WS_PIN,
    .data_out_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
    .data_in_num = I2S_DIN_PIN
  };

  if (i2s_driver_install(I2S_PORT, &i2s_config, 0, NULL) != ESP_OK ||
      i2s_set_pin(I2S_PORT, &pin_config) != ESP_OK) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Record stereo to PSRAM
  Serial.printf("\nRecording %d seconds (stereo)...\n\n", RECORD_DURATION);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
  delay(500);

  if (!recordStereoToPSRAM()) {
    Serial.println("\nRecording FAILED!");
    error_blink();
  }

  Serial.println("\n========================================");
  Serial.println("Stereo recording complete!");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  // Downmix to mono
  Serial.print("Downmixing stereo to mono... ");
  downmixToMono();
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Write to SD card
  Serial.print("\nInitializing SD card... ");
  SPI.begin(SD_SCK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS);
  if (!SD.begin(SD_CS)) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  Serial.print("Writing mono WAV to SD... ");
  if (!writeMonoToSD()) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK\n");

  Serial.println("========================================");
  Serial.println("SUCCESS!");
  Serial.println("========================================");
  Serial.println("\nMono file: /recording_mono.wav");
  Serial.println("Remove SD card and play on computer!");

  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
}

void loop() {
  delay(1000);
}

bool recordStereoToPSRAM() {
  uint32_t samples_written = 0;
  uint32_t last_percent = 0;
  unsigned long start_time = millis();

  while (samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES) {
    // Blink LED
    if ((millis() / 200) % 2 == 0) {
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
    } else {
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
    }

    // Read I2S
    size_t bytes_read = 0;
    if (i2s_read(I2S_PORT, i2s_buffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(int32_t),
                 &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY) != ESP_OK) {
      Serial.println("\nI2S read error");
      return false;
    }

    // Convert and store
    int samples_read = bytes_read / sizeof(int32_t);
    for (int i = 0; i < samples_read && samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES; i++) {
      stereo_buffer[samples_written++] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);
    }

    // Progress
    uint32_t percent = (samples_written * 100) / STEREO_SAMPLES;
    if (percent != last_percent && percent % 10 == 0) {
      Serial.printf("Progress: %u%% (%u / %u samples)\n",
                    percent, samples_written, STEREO_SAMPLES);
      last_percent = percent;
    }
  }

  Serial.printf("\nRecorded: %u samples in %lu ms\n", samples_written, millis() - start_time);
  return true;
}

void downmixToMono() {
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];      // Even indices = left
    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1]; // Odd indices = right

    #ifdef SIMPLE_AVERAGE
    // Standard (L + R) / 2
    mono_buffer[i] = ((int32_t)left + (int32_t)right) / 2;

    #elif defined(PEAK_SELECT)
    // Take the sample with larger absolute value
    if (abs(left) > abs(right)) {
      mono_buffer[i] = left;
    } else {
      mono_buffer[i] = right;
    }

    #elif defined(ADAPTIVE_MIX)
    // Track energy of each channel
    left_energy = left_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(left) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
    right_energy = right_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(right) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);

    // Calculate weights (favor channel with more energy)
    float total_energy = left_energy + right_energy;
    float left_weight = (total_energy > 0) ? (left_energy / total_energy) : 0.5f;
    float right_weight = 1.0f - left_weight;

    // Weighted mix
    mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight);

    #else
    #error "No downmix algorithm selected! Uncomment one: SIMPLE_AVERAGE, PEAK_SELECT, or ADAPTIVE_MIX"
    #endif
  }
}

bool writeMonoToSD() {
  File file = SD.open("/recording_mono.wav", FILE_WRITE);
  if (!file) return false;

  // Write WAV header (MONO)
  writeWavHeader(file, MONO_DATA_SIZE, 1);  // 1 channel = mono

  // Write mono buffer
  size_t written = file.write((uint8_t*)mono_buffer, MONO_DATA_SIZE);
  file.close();

  return (written == MONO_DATA_SIZE);
}

void writeWavHeader(File &file, uint32_t data_size, uint16_t channels) {
  // RIFF header
  file.write((uint8_t*)"RIFF", 4);
  uint32_t file_size = data_size + 36;
  writeLittleEndian(file, file_size, 4);
  file.write((uint8_t*)"WAVE", 4);

  // fmt chunk
  file.write((uint8_t*)"fmt ", 4);
  writeLittleEndian(file, 16, 4);                    // Chunk size
  writeLittleEndian(file, 1, 2);                     // PCM
  writeLittleEndian(file, channels, 2);              // Channels (1=mono, 2=stereo)
  writeLittleEndian(file, SAMPLE_RATE, 4);           // Sample rate
  writeLittleEndian(file, SAMPLE_RATE * channels * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8), 4); // Byte rate
  writeLittleEndian(file, channels * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8), 2); // Block align
  writeLittleEndian(file, BITS_PER_SAMPLE, 2);       // Bits per sample

  // data chunk
  file.write((uint8_t*)"data", 4);
  writeLittleEndian(file, data_size, 4);
}

void writeLittleEndian(File &file, uint32_t value, int bytes) {
  for (int i = 0; i < bytes; i++) {
    file.write((uint8_t)(value & 0xFF));
    value >>= 8;
  }
}

void error_blink() {
  while(1) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(200);
  }
}

```md
# Dual Microphone to Mono Downmix Recording

## Overview

This sketch captures audio from **two INMP441 microphones** and intelligently downmixes them to **MONO** for clearer voice capture than using a single microphone alone.

## Why Dual Mics → Mono?

✅ **Better spatial coverage** - Captures voice from multiple directions
✅ **Noise reduction** - Two mics can reject environmental noise better
✅ **Clearer speech** - Combined signal is more robust than single mic
✅ **No stereo "ping-pong"** - Voice stays centered, not split between channels

## Hardware Wiring

**Same as stereo setup:**

\```
ESP32-S3-LCD-2          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)      INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
────────────────        ─────────────────      ──────────────────
3.3V ───────────┬────── VDD                    VDD
                │
GND ────────────┼────── GND ──────────┬─────── GND
                │                     │
GPIO 2 (BCK) ───┼────── SCK ──────────┼─────── SCK
GPIO 4 (WS) ────┼────── WS ───────────┼─────── WS
GPIO 18 (DIN) ──┴────── SD ───────────┴─────── SD
                        │                      │
                        L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
\```

## Downmix Algorithms

The sketch provides **three algorithms** - choose one by uncommenting it in the code:

### 1. SIMPLE_AVERAGE (Default - Recommended)

\```cpp
#define SIMPLE_AVERAGE
\```

**Formula:** `Mono = (Left + Right) / 2`

**Best for:**
- Mics positioned close together
- Voice directly between the mics
- General-purpose recording

**Pros:**
- Standard industry approach
- Maintains proper loudness
- Smooth, natural sound

**Cons:**
- May have phase cancellation if mics are far apart
- Can reduce volume if signals are out of phase

---

### 2. PEAK_SELECT

\```cpp
// #define SIMPLE_AVERAGE    // Comment out
#define PEAK_SELECT          // Uncomment this
\```

**Formula:** `Mono = max(abs(L), abs(R))` (preserves sign)

**Best for:**
- Noisy environments
- Preventing phase cancellation
- When mic placement causes phase issues

**Pros:**
- No phase cancellation
- Always takes the stronger signal
- Good for speech in noise

**Cons:**
- Can sound slightly harsher
- May amplify brief noises

---

### 3. ADAPTIVE_MIX (Most Intelligent)

\```cpp
// #define SIMPLE_AVERAGE    // Comment out
#define ADAPTIVE_MIX         // Uncomment this
\```

**Formula:** Weighted average based on recent signal strength

\```
left_weight = left_energy / (left_energy + right_energy)
Mono = Left * left_weight + Right * (1 - left_weight)
\```

**Best for:**
- Moving speaker
- Voice from varying positions
- Professional-quality capture

**Pros:**
- Automatically favors the mic with better signal
- Adapts to speaker movement
- Best overall quality

**Cons:**
- Slightly more CPU usage (negligible on ESP32-S3)

---

## Output File

- **Format:** WAV (PCM)
- **Sample Rate:** 16000 Hz
- **Channels:** 1 (MONO)
- **Bit Depth:** 16-bit
- **Duration:** 30 seconds
- **File Size:** ~960 KB (half of stereo)
- **Location:** SD card `/recording_mono.wav`

## How It Works

1. **Record stereo** from both mics to PSRAM (no SD interference)
2. **Downmix** stereo to mono using selected algorithm
3. **Write mono WAV** to SD card
4. **Done!** LED stays solid ON

## Usage

1. **Wire both microphones** as shown above
2. **Insert SD card** (FAT32 formatted)
3. **Choose algorithm** in the sketch (uncomment one `#define`)
4. **Upload** to ESP32-S3-LCD-2
5. **Wait 30 seconds** for recording (LED blinks)
6. **Remove SD card** and play `/recording_mono.wav`

## Recommended Testing

Try all three algorithms with your setup to see which sounds best!

### Test Process:

1. Upload with `SIMPLE_AVERAGE`
2. Record, rename file to `test_average.wav`
3. Change to `PEAK_SELECT`, upload, record
4. Rename to `test_peak.wav`
5. Change to `ADAPTIVE_MIX`, upload, record
6. Rename to `test_adaptive.wav`
7. **Compare on your computer** - pick the clearest one!

## Expected Results

**SIMPLE_AVERAGE:**
Smooth, natural sound. Best for most cases.

**PEAK_SELECT:**
Slightly louder, more present. Good if you hear phase issues with SIMPLE_AVERAGE.

**ADAPTIVE_MIX:**
Most "intelligent" - follows your voice position. Best if you move around.

## Troubleshooting

### "Mono sounds quieter than stereo"
- This is normal - stereo has two channels
- SIMPLE_AVERAGE maintains proper volume
- Try PEAK_SELECT for louder output

### "Still hear phase cancellation / hollow sound"
- Switch to `PEAK_SELECT` or `ADAPTIVE_MIX`
- Check mic spacing (closer = less phase issues)
- Ensure both mics face the same direction

### "One mic still dominates"
- Try `ADAPTIVE_MIX` - it adapts to signal strength
- Check wiring - both mics should be equal distance from voice source

## Technical References

Based on research from:
- **Standard downmix:** (L + R) / 2 is industry standard ([Best practices for Stereo-to-Mono mixdown](https://www.audiokinetic.com/qa/5408/best-practices-for-stereo-to-mono-mixdown))
- **Phase considerations:** Important for microphone arrays ([Intelligent downmix of stereo to mono](https://sound.stackexchange.com/questions/39151/intelligent-downmix-of-stereo-to-mono))
- **Beamforming techniques:** ESP32-S3 dual mic processing ([Beamforming & DoA on ESP32-S3](https://prometeo.blog/en/practical-case-beamforming-doa-on-esp32-s3-i2s-inmp441/))
- **ESP-Skainet:** Espressif's speech SDK with noise reduction and beamforming ([ESP Audio DevKits](https://www.espressif.com/en/products/devkits/esp-audio-devkits))

## Next Steps

Once you find the best algorithm for your use case:
- Integrate with voice recognition
- Add voice activity detection (VAD)
- Implement real-time streaming
- Combine with speaker output for full duplex

---

**Pro Tip:** For best results, position mics 5-10cm apart, both facing the speaker!

   271→void downmixSimpleAverage() {
   272→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   273→    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
   274→    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];

   276→    // Standard (L + R) / 2

   280→
   281→void downmixPeakSelect() {
   282→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   283→    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
   284→    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
   285→
   286→    // Take the sample with larger absolute value
   287→    if (abs(left) > abs(right)) {
   288→      mono_buffer[i] = left;
   289→    } else {
   290→      mono_buffer[i] = right;
   291→    }
   292→  }
   293→}
   294→
   295→void downmixAdaptive() {
   296→  float left_energy = 0.0f;
   297→  float right_energy = 0.0f;
   298→  const float ENERGY_DECAY = 0.95f;
   299→
   300→  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
   301→    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
   302→    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
   303→
   304→    // Track energy of each channel
   305→    left_energy = left_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(left) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
   306→    right_energy = right_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(right) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
   307→
   308→    // Calculate weights (favor channel with more energy)
   309→    float total_energy = left_energy + right_energy;
   310→    float left_weight = (total_energy > 0) ? (left_energy / total_energy) : 0.5f;
   311→    float right_weight = 1.0f - left_weight;
   312→
   313→    // Weighted mix
   314→    mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight);
   315→  }
   316→}

right_energy = decay * right_energy + (1-decay) * abs(right)

left_weight = left_energy / total
right_weight = right_energy / total

right_weight = 1.0 - left_weight

## 🎯 The New HYBRID_MIX Algorithm

**How it works:**
```
1. Tracks energy of both channels (like ADAPTIVE)
2. Calculates adaptive weights (like ADAPTIVE)
3. BUT constrains weights to 30%-70% range
   - Left channel: minimum 30%, maximum 70%
   - Right channel: minimum 30%, maximum 70%
4. Both channels ALWAYS contribute
```

**What this gives you:**

✅ **Adaptive's loudness & clarity** - Still favors the stronger signal  
✅ **Average's width & fullness** - Both mics always active (30% minimum)  
✅ **No interruption** - When you block a mic, it drops to 30%, not 0%  
✅ **Less noise than pure average** - Still intelligently weights toward cleaner signal

- Loudest and clearest
- Follows your voice
- "Interrupted" when blocking mic

### 3. `/recording_hybrid.wav` - **🎯 BEST OF BOTH**
- 30-70% adaptive weighting  
- **Clarity + Width combined**
- No interruption
- Should be the winner!

- The width and fullness you love from AVERAGE

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent:

**Initial Request**: Create a dual INMP441 microphone test that records 30 seconds of stereo audio and saves to SD card, based on the working single_mic_test. Required pin layout documentation and SD card storage (not internal flash).

**Evolution**: After stereo recording worked but had "fighting" between channels when speaking in the middle, user requested a mono downmix version that uses both mics to capture clearer mono audio than a single mic alone.

**Final Request**: Create comparison of three downmix algorithms (SIMPLE_AVERAGE, ADAPTIVE_MIX, HYBRID_MIX), removing PEAK_SELECT after testing showed it was bad. HYBRID_MIX should combine adaptive's clarity with average's width by constraining weights to 30%-70% range.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts:

- **INMP441 MEMS Microphones**: I2S digital microphones with L/R channel selection pin
- **I2S Protocol**: Stereo audio capture with interleaved L/R samples, 32-bit words containing 24-bit data
- **L/R Pin Configuration**: L/R → GND = LEFT channel, L/R → VDD = RIGHT channel (verified via web search)
- **PSRAM Buffering**: Recording to PSRAM first eliminates SD card write timing interference with I2S capture
- **WAV File Format**: RIFF/WAVE headers with PCM format, proper little-endian encoding
- **Stereo-to-Mono Downmixing Algorithms**:
  - Simple Average: (L+R)/2 - industry standard
  - Adaptive Mix: Weighted average based on signal energy tracking
  - Hybrid Mix: Adaptive with 30%-70% weight constraints to maintain width
- **SD Card vs FFat**: SD card (removable storage) vs FFat (internal flash partition)
- **ESP32-S3 PSRAM**: 8MB OPI PSRAM for large buffer allocation

```cpp
// PSRAM buffer allocation
psram_buffer = (int16_t*)ps_malloc(WAV_DATA_SIZE);

// Recording loop to PSRAM
while (samples_written < TOTAL_SAMPLES) {
  i2s_read(I2S_PORT, i2s_buffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(int32_t), &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY);
  for (int i = 0; i < samples_read; i++) {
    psram_buffer[samples_written++] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);
  }
}

// Write to SD after recording complete
File file = SD.open("/recording.wav", FILE_WRITE);
writeWavHeader(file, WAV_DATA_SIZE);
file.write((uint8_t*)psram_buffer, WAV_DATA_SIZE);
```

### `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/tests/dual_mic_sd_record/WIRING_GUIDE.md`

### `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/tests/dual_mono_record/dual_mono_record.ino`
- **Why created**: User wanted mono downmix from stereo for clearer voice capture
- **Multiple iterations**: 
  1. Originally single algorithm selection
  2. Modified to generate all 3 algorithms in one run
  3. Final version: Removed PEAK_SELECT, added HYBRID_MIX
  
- **Final algorithm implementations**:

```cpp
// 1. SIMPLE_AVERAGE - Standard (L+R)/2
void downmixSimpleAverage() {
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
    mono_buffer[i] = ((int32_t)left + (int32_t)right) / 2;
  }
}

// 2. ADAPTIVE_MIX - Intelligent weighted mix
void downmixAdaptive() {
  float left_energy = 0.0f;
  float right_energy = 0.0f;
  const float ENERGY_DECAY = 0.95f;
  
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
    
    left_energy = left_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(left) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
    right_energy = right_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(right) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
    
    float total_energy = left_energy + right_energy;
    float left_weight = (total_energy > 0) ? (left_energy / total_energy) : 0.5f;
    float right_weight = 1.0f - left_weight;
    
    mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight);
  }
}

// 3. HYBRID_MIX - Best of both (clarity + width)
void downmixHybrid() {
  float left_energy = 0.0f;
  float right_energy = 0.0f;
  const float ENERGY_DECAY = 0.95f;
  const float MIN_WEIGHT = 0.30f;  // Minimum 30% per channel
  const float MAX_WEIGHT = 0.70f;  // Maximum 70% per channel
  
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];
    
    left_energy = left_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(left) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
    right_energy = right_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(right) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
    
    float total_energy = left_energy + right_energy;
    float left_weight = (total_energy > 0) ? (left_energy / total_energy) : 0.5f;
    
    // Constrain to 30%-70% range
    if (left_weight < MIN_WEIGHT) left_weight = MIN_WEIGHT;
    if (left_weight > MAX_WEIGHT) left_weight = MAX_WEIGHT;
    
    float right_weight = 1.0f - left_weight;
    mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight);
  }
}
```

- **Output files**: Creates 3 WAV files on SD card:
  - `/recording_average.wav` - Wide, full sound
  - `/recording_adaptive.wav` - Loud & clear
  - `/recording_hybrid.wav` - Clarity + Width (best of both)

### `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/tests/dual_mono_record/README.md`

## 8. Current Work:

Just completed replacing PEAK_SELECT with HYBRID_MIX algorithm in `/home/alphons/project/OAISYS25/badge/workbench/tests/dual_mono_record/dual_mono_record.ino`.

The HYBRID_MIX algorithm was designed based on user's feedback that they wanted "adaptive's loudness, clarity, sound depth" combined with "the width of sound in average" while avoiding the "interrupted" feeling when blocking a mic and reducing background noise.

**Implementation details**:
- Removed `downmixPeakSelect()` function entirely
- Added `downmixHybrid()` function with 30%-70% weight constraints
- Updated setup() to call all three algorithms in sequence
- Modified file output names and descriptions:
  - `/recording_average.wav` - Wide, full sound

  - `/recording_hybrid.wav` - Clarity + Width!

**Key code change**:
```cpp
void downmixHybrid() {
  const float MIN_WEIGHT = 0.30f;  // Minimum 30% per channel (max 70%)
  const float MAX_WEIGHT = 0.70f;
  
  // ... adaptive energy tracking ...
  
  // Constrain to 30%-70% range (maintains "width" while keeping clarity)
  if (left_weight < MIN_WEIGHT) left_weight = MIN_WEIGHT;
  if (left_weight > MAX_WEIGHT) left_weight = MAX_WEIGHT;
  
  // Weighted mix
  mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight);
}
```

This ensures both channels always contribute at least 30%, preventing the "interruption" issue while still intelligently favoring the stronger signal for clarity.

I found comprehensive information about connecting the MAX98357A I2S amplifier to an ESP32. Here's what you need to know:

## Pin Connections

The three important pins are BCLK, DIN, and LRC, where DIN is the data input pin and LRC is the Left-Right Channel selection pin.

### Common ESP32 to MAX98357A Wiring Examples:

**Example 1 (from DFRobot):**
LRC to ESP32 GPIO 26, BCLK to ESP32 GPIO 25, DIN to ESP32 GPIO 14

**Example 2 (from Circuit Digest):**
BCLK to GPIO 27, LRC (Word Select) to GPIO 26, DIN (Serial Data) to GPIO 25

**Example 3 (from Forum):**
DIN to GPIO22, BCLK to GPIO26, LRC to GPIO25

### Power Connections:
- **VIN**: Connect to 3.3V or 5V on ESP32 (supports 3.3V-5V power supply)
- **GND**: Connect to ESP32 GND

### Important Notes:

1. **SD Pin Confusion**: Be careful not to confuse the pin labelled SD with the Serial Data pin - this pin is actually the Shutdown and channel select pin. Use the DIN pin for the serial data.

2. **Pin Flexibility**: The GPIO pins used for I2S can vary - ESP32 allows flexible pin assignment for I2S peripherals, so you can use different GPIOs as long as they're configured correctly in your code.

3. **Speaker Connection**: You must use a speaker with 4 to 8-ohm voice coils, and the speaker connects directly to the amplifier's SPK+ and SPK- terminals.

The key is ensuring your code initializes the I2S interface with the same GPIO pins you've physically wired.

/*
 * Record, Downmix, and Playback Loop
 *
 * Records 30 seconds of stereo audio from dual INMP441 microphones,
 * downmixes to mono using HYBRID algorithm, then loops playback
 * through MAX98357A speaker.
 *
 * Hardware:
 * =========
 * INMP441 Microphones (I2S0 RX):
 *   Mic #1 (LEFT):  L/R -> GND
 *   Mic #2 (RIGHT): L/R -> 3.3V
 *   Both share: BCK=GPIO2, WS=GPIO4, DIN=GPIO18
 *
 * MAX98357A Speaker (I2S1 TX):
 *   VIN  -> 5V (or 3.3V)
 *   GND  -> GND
 *   BCLK -> GPIO 6
 *   LRC  -> GPIO 7
 *   DIN  -> GPIO 8
 *   GAIN -> Float (9dB), GND (12dB), or VDD (15dB)
 *
 * Behavior:
 * =========
 * 1. Records 30 seconds stereo to PSRAM
 * 2. Downmixes to mono using HYBRID algorithm
 * 3. Loops playback forever
 *
 * LED Feedback:
 * =============
 * - Blinking during recording
 * - Solid ON during playback
 */

#include <driver/i2s.h>

// Microphone pins (I2S0)
#define MIC_BCK_PIN    2
#define MIC_WS_PIN     4
#define MIC_DIN_PIN    18

// Speaker pins (I2S1)
#define SPK_BCK_PIN    6
#define SPK_WS_PIN     7
#define SPK_DOUT_PIN   8

// Recording configuration
#define SAMPLE_RATE       16000
#define BITS_PER_SAMPLE   16
#define RECORD_DURATION   30
#define BUFFER_SIZE       2048

// Calculate sizes
const uint32_t STEREO_SAMPLES = SAMPLE_RATE * 2 * RECORD_DURATION;
const uint32_t MONO_SAMPLES = SAMPLE_RATE * RECORD_DURATION;
const uint32_t MONO_DATA_SIZE = MONO_SAMPLES * (BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8);

// LED
#define LED_PIN 1

// Buffers in PSRAM
int32_t i2s_buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
int16_t* stereo_buffer = nullptr;
int16_t* mono_buffer = nullptr;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  delay(1000);

  pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);

  Serial.println("\n========================================");
  Serial.println("Record -> Downmix -> Playback Loop");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  // Check PSRAM
  Serial.printf("Total PSRAM: %u bytes\n", ESP.getPsramSize());
  Serial.printf("Free PSRAM: %u bytes\n\n", ESP.getFreePsram());

  // Allocate stereo buffer
  uint32_t stereo_bytes = STEREO_SAMPLES * sizeof(int16_t);
  Serial.printf("Allocating stereo buffer (%u bytes)... ", stereo_bytes);
  stereo_buffer = (int16_t*)ps_malloc(stereo_bytes);
  if (!stereo_buffer) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Allocate mono buffer
  Serial.printf("Allocating mono buffer (%u bytes)... ", MONO_DATA_SIZE);
  mono_buffer = (int16_t*)ps_malloc(MONO_DATA_SIZE);
  if (!mono_buffer) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK\n");

  // Initialize I2S0 for microphones (RX)
  Serial.print("Initializing I2S0 (microphones)... ");
  i2s_config_t mic_config = {
    .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX),
    .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
    .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,
    .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_RIGHT_LEFT,
    .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
    .intr_alloc_flags = ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1,
    .dma_buf_count = 4,
    .dma_buf_len = 1024,
    .use_apll = false,
    .tx_desc_auto_clear = false,
    .fixed_mclk = 0
  };

  i2s_pin_config_t mic_pins = {
    .bck_io_num = MIC_BCK_PIN,
    .ws_io_num = MIC_WS_PIN,
    .data_out_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
    .data_in_num = MIC_DIN_PIN
  };

  if (i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &mic_config, 0, NULL) != ESP_OK ||
      i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_0, &mic_pins) != ESP_OK) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK");

  // Initialize I2S1 for speaker (TX)
  Serial.print("Initializing I2S1 (speaker)... ");
  i2s_config_t spk_config = {
    .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_TX),
    .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
    .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_16BIT,
    .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,  // Mono
    .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
    .intr_alloc_flags = ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1,
    .dma_buf_count = 4,
    .dma_buf_len = 512,
    .use_apll = false,
    .tx_desc_auto_clear = true,
    .fixed_mclk = 0
  };

  i2s_pin_config_t spk_pins = {
    .bck_io_num = SPK_BCK_PIN,
    .ws_io_num = SPK_WS_PIN,
    .data_out_num = SPK_DOUT_PIN,
    .data_in_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE
  };

  if (i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_1, &spk_config, 0, NULL) != ESP_OK ||
      i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_1, &spk_pins) != ESP_OK) {
    Serial.println("FAILED");
    error_blink();
  }
  Serial.println("OK\n");

  // Record stereo
  Serial.printf("Recording %d seconds (stereo)...\n\n", RECORD_DURATION);
  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
  delay(500);

  if (!recordStereoToPSRAM()) {
    Serial.println("\nRecording FAILED!");
    error_blink();
  }

  Serial.println("\n========================================");
  Serial.println("Recording complete!");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  // Downmix to mono using HYBRID
  Serial.print("Applying HYBRID downmix... ");
  downmixHybrid();
  Serial.println("OK\n");

  Serial.println("========================================");
  Serial.println("Starting playback loop...");
  Serial.println("========================================\n");

  digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
}

void loop() {
  playMonoBuffer();
}

bool recordStereoToPSRAM() {
  uint32_t samples_written = 0;
  uint32_t last_percent = 0;
  unsigned long start_time = millis();

  while (samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES) {
    // Blink LED
    if ((millis() / 200) % 2 == 0) {
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
    } else {
      digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
    }

    // Read I2S
    size_t bytes_read = 0;
    if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(int32_t),
                 &bytes_read, portMAX_DELAY) != ESP_OK) {
      return false;
    }

    // Convert and store
    int samples_read = bytes_read / sizeof(int32_t);
    for (int i = 0; i < samples_read && samples_written < STEREO_SAMPLES; i++) {
      stereo_buffer[samples_written++] = (int16_t)(i2s_buffer[i] >> 16);
    }

    // Progress
    uint32_t percent = (samples_written * 100) / STEREO_SAMPLES;
    if (percent != last_percent && percent % 10 == 0) {
      Serial.printf("Progress: %u%% (%u / %u samples)\n",
                    percent, samples_written, STEREO_SAMPLES);
      last_percent = percent;
    }
  }

  Serial.printf("\nRecorded: %u samples in %lu ms\n", samples_written, millis() - start_time);
  return true;
}

void downmixHybrid() {
  float left_energy = 0.0f;
  float right_energy = 0.0f;
  const float ENERGY_DECAY = 0.95f;
  const float MIN_WEIGHT = 0.30f;  // Minimum 30% per channel
  const float MAX_WEIGHT = 0.70f;  // Maximum 70% per channel

  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i++) {
    int16_t left = stereo_buffer[i * 2];
    int16_t right = stereo_buffer[i * 2 + 1];

    // Track energy of each channel
    left_energy = left_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(left) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);
    right_energy = right_energy * ENERGY_DECAY + abs(right) * (1.0f - ENERGY_DECAY);

    // Calculate raw weights
    float total_energy = left_energy + right_energy;
    float left_weight = (total_energy > 0) ? (left_energy / total_energy) : 0.5f;

    // Constrain to 30%-70% range
    if (left_weight < MIN_WEIGHT) left_weight = MIN_WEIGHT;
    if (left_weight > MAX_WEIGHT) left_weight = MAX_WEIGHT;

    float right_weight = 1.0f - left_weight;

    // Weighted mix
    mono_buffer[i] = (int16_t)(left * left_weight + right * right_weight);
  }
}

void playMonoBuffer() {
  size_t bytes_written = 0;
  static unsigned long last_print = 0;

  // Play entire mono buffer
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < MONO_SAMPLES; i += BUFFER_SIZE) {
    uint32_t samples_to_write = min((uint32_t)BUFFER_SIZE, MONO_SAMPLES - i);

    i2s_write(I2S_NUM_1, &mono_buffer[i], samples_to_write * sizeof(int16_t),
              &bytes_written, portMAX_DELAY);

    // Print status every ~2 seconds
    if (millis() - last_print > 2000) {
      Serial.printf("Playing... sample %u / %u\n", i, MONO_SAMPLES);
      last_print = millis();
    }
  }

  Serial.println("Playback complete, looping...\n");
}

void error_blink() {
  while(1) {
    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
    delay(200);
  }
}
